title: The Rebel base is chosen secretly
text: During setup the Rebel player secretly picks the system of his base; its probe card lies facedown under the "Location" space of the board. The base starts hidden and may be revealed later.

title: The "Rebel Base" space is not a system
text: The "Rebel Base" space on the board is separate from the base's system and is not a system. Units can be built from and deployed to it as if it were a system and can move to and from it by special rules; missions cannot be attempted or resolved there unless a card says so; it cannot gain or lose loyalty.

title: Units on the Rebel Base space are outside every system
text: While the base is hidden, units on the "Rebel Base" space are not in the base's system: they do not fight there and do not count as Rebel units in that system. Only when the base is revealed are they placed into the system.
rationale: RR p.10 says the space is not a system and RR p.11 says that on reveal the units on the space are placed in the base's system, which only makes sense if they were not there before. No source spells out the consequences for combat or victory explicitly.

title: Moving to and from the Rebel Base space
text: While the base is hidden, Rebel units on the "Rebel Base" space may move to the base's system or to a system adjacent to it. Moving to or from the space therefore tells the Empire the base is in, or next to, that system. A few missions move units between the space and any system.

Moving To and From the Rebel Base

title: Activating the Rebel Base space
text: The Rebel player may activate the "Rebel Base" space to move units onto it from the base's system or from systems adjacent to the base's system.

sources.section: Moving to or from the Rebel Base

title: A leader on the Rebel Base space locks only that space
text: A leader on the "Rebel Base" space prevents units from moving out of that space, but does not stop units that stand in the base's system.

sources.section: Moving to or from the Rebel Base

title: When the Rebel base must be revealed
text: Whenever the Empire has loyalty or ground units in the Rebel base's system, the Rebel player must reveal the base. The condition is checked at any time, not only after movement.

sources.quote: If the Imperial player ever has loyalty or ground units in the Rebel base’s system

exceptions.text: Imperial ships alone, including the Death Star and the Death Star Under Construction, never reveal the base.
Probe cards and the Imperial Long Range Probe mission never reveal the base.

title: Revealing the base after Imperial ground units move in
text: When Imperial ground units move into a system, the Rebel player must declare whether his base is there; if so, it is revealed after all movement of the activation and before combat.

title: Imperial ships alone do not reveal the base
text: If the Empire has ships but no ground units in a system, the base is not revealed and the Rebel player gives no information about whether the base is there.

title: The Death Star does not reveal the base
text: A Death Star or Death Star Under Construction in the same system as the hidden base does not reveal it: ships, including the Death Star, never reveal the base; only Imperial ground units or Imperial loyalty in the base's system do (RR p.11).

title: How the base is revealed
text: To reveal, the Rebel player turns the probe card from the "Location" space faceup and puts it on the "Rebel Base" space, where it stays as a reminder. All units and leaders on the "Rebel Base" space are placed in the system shown on that card.

title: Voluntary reveal
text: The Rebel player may choose to reveal his base during one of his Command Phase turns (timing narrowed by the FAQ errata).

title: Voluntary reveal only at the start of a Rebel turn (errata)
text: The Rebel player can reveal his base voluntarily only at the start of one of his Command Phase turns, before he uses a leader or passes.

title: No voluntary reveal after passing
text: Once the Rebel player has passed he takes no more turns this phase, so he cannot reveal the base voluntarily.

title: Revealing the base next to Imperial units starts combat
text: If the Rebel player reveals his base on his turn while Imperial units are already in that system, combat is resolved immediately.

title: While the base is revealed
text: Units can no longer be deployed to or moved to the "Rebel Base" space; anything that would be placed there goes to the base's system instead. Cards that refer to the space apply to the base's system. The space's resource icons still work unless an Imperial unit or Imperial loyalty is in the base's system.

title: Deploying to a revealed base system
text: After the base is revealed, the Rebel player may deploy units to its system only if he has loyalty there and there are no Imperial units in it; a remote or neutral base system receives no deployments.

title: Establishing a new base
text: The Rapid Mobilization mission, resolved at the end of the Command Phase, lets the Rebel player draw four probe cards and pick one as his new base; it cannot be a system with Imperial loyalty, Imperial units or a destroyed marker. The old base is revealed, units and leaders from the space go to the old system and its probe card goes to the Empire. Unchosen cards go to the bottom of the probe deck.
